newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk cb buys lira for dlrs in late trade - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turk cb buys lira for dlrs in late trade - bankers.

text.p: Turkish central bank began buying lira for dollars in late trade on Thursday to guard the domestic currency amid political uncertainty, bankers said.
The lira firmed to 145,900 against the dollar after the intervention from previous 145,990. MORE EKS
The lira had earlier eased from Wednesday's 145,500 close in line with a firmer dollar/mark parity and the overnight cost of funding.
Bankers said there was no unusual demand for the U.S. currency as search for a new government began after the Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned late on Wednesday.
"The central bank is trying to keep the lira depreciation in line with its end-month target of around five percent against the currency basket composed of dollar and mark," said one banker.

Bankers said as an early warning, the central bank kept its key dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 145,300 lira, much lower than banks' dollar bids which rose to 145,990, reflecting the parity and cost of funding adjustments.
So the bank intervened when the gap between its key rate and banks' dollar bids rose to 0.47 percent from Thursday's 0.4 percent, they added.
